catalog_quote: [Toliver 2008:52] Se puede saber que en el segundo caso la partícula es ligada por la colocación de la fuerza de la voz que en quechua recae en la penúltima sílaba: a.'li.cag / NO 'a.li # cag [Toliver 2008:56, 4.1.2 Patrón silábico, item 2 + fn. 2] La cantidad vocálica representa una consonante (y aparece solamente en la coda); es decir, V: = [V] [C]. ... Ver el primer artículo de este volumen “La interpretación de las vocales largas en el quechua” por Weber y Landerman. [Weber & Landerman 2008:25-26, section 3] En la mayoría de las variedades centrales del quechua, el acento se asigna a la penúltima sílaba. Por ejemplo: [aywá:pis] /aywa-:-pis/ ‘yo también voy’ [aywaša:píta] /aywa-ša-:-pita/ ‘desde que fui’ En esos dialectos, la vocal larga que funciona como marcador de primera persona se acentúa cuando está en posición final de palabra: [aywá:] /aywa-:/ ‘voy’ En la variedad del Huallaga y algunas otras variedades, también se acentúan las vocales largas finales que tienen otra procedencia: ... Según el análisis V: = [V][V], la regla de colocación del acento podría formularse así: “Acentúese la penúltima vocal”. Para las interpretaciones V: = [V, +largo] y V: = [V][C], se necesitarían otras especificaciones para acentuar las vocales largas en posición final.

new_statements.quote: El quechua posee una forma cag que puede traducirse como ‘eso que es’. [...] su uso común con ciertas palabras como ali ‘bueno’ lo ha convertido en una forma ligada. nogapag cag ‘lo que es para mí’ (partícula libre) / alicag ‘el que es bueno, el bueno’ (partícula ligada). Se puede saber que en el segundo caso la partícula es ligada por la colocación de la fuerza de la voz que en quechua recae en la penúltima sílaba: a.'li.cag NO 'a.li # cag [p.50: Cabe anotar que los datos (vea el apéndice) corresponden principalmente a las variedades que se hablan en el departamento de Huánuco, especialmente las variedades de Ambo-Pasco, Margos-Yarowilca-Lauricocha (MYL) y Huamalíes.]
new_statements.translation: Quechua has a form cag 'that which is' ... its common use with certain words such as ali 'good' has turned it into a bound form: nogapag cag 'what is for me' (free particle) / alicag 'the one that is good' (bound particle). One can tell that in the second case the particle is bound from the placement of stress ('the force of the voice'), which in Quechua falls on the penultimate syllable: a.'li.cag, NOT 'a.li # cag. [p.50: The data correspond principally to the varieties spoken in the department of Huánuco, especially Ambo-Pasco, Margos-Yarowilca-Lauricocha and Huamalíes.]

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress falls on the penultimate syllable of the (phonological) word; a clitic/suffix that becomes bound counts toward the word, shifting stress rightward (a.'li.cag vs. 'a.li + cag).
new_statements.exceptions: None in Toliver's chapter. The companion chapter in the same volume (Weber & Landerman 2008: 25-26) notes for central Quechua generally that a word-final long vowel (e.g. 1st-person -V:) attracts stress to the final syllable, and that Huallaga also stresses other final long vowels; not stated specifically for Ambo-Pasco.
new_statements.domain_note: Word domain incl. bound particles/enclitics (the example uses stress placement as a diagnostic of boundness). Passing remark in a loan-phonology article, phrased for 'quechua' in general by the Ambo-Pasco field linguist; data principally Ambo-Pasco (p.50).
new_statements.identity_note: Toliver's 2008 loanword/nickname article states (p.50) that its data 'corresponden principalmente a las variedades que se hablan en el departamento de Huánuco, especialmente las variedades de Ambo-Pasco, Margos-Yarowilca-Lauricocha (MYL) y Huamalíes'; the stress remark on p.52 is phrased for 'quechua' generally and the example a.'li.cag is in Ambo-Pasco orthography (g = voiced postvelar). Toliver is the SIL field linguist for Ambo-Pasco [qva] (provinces of Ambo, Huánuco and Pasco, Pasco). No dedicated phonology of ambo1252 was found; the statement is a passing first-hand remark, not a stress section.

new_statements.quote: In most Quechua dialects stress is assigned to the penultimate vowel of each polysyllabic word form and thus provides an easy phonology-based criterion for word delimitation. Exceptionally, in interjections and emphatic expressions, stress can be word-final, e.g. in alaláw ‘how cold!’. [...] In the Quechua I dialects stress is maintained in word-final position when the long vowel morpheme referring to first-person subject or possessor is immediately followed by a word boundary. (Length oppositions not connected with the first-person morpheme are normally neutralised in word-final position, in which case stress is regularly assigned to the penultimate syllable.)

new_statements.relation_note: Compatible with the catalog record (Toliver 2008: penultimate 'fuerza de la voz'; Weber & Landerman 2008: long vowel = VC, final long-vowel stress): Adelaar states the same penultimate default and adds, for Quechua I as a whole, the word-final stress on the first-person long-vowel morpheme and emphatic final stress. The statement is family/branch-level: Ambo-Pasco is not named; it falls under Torero's quantity-insensitive 'Yaru' subgroup (p.185, Andean sector of Pasco) / Alto Huallaga (Huánuco), for which no separate stress remark is made. No weight-driven pattern of the Ancash type is attributed to Yaru.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Across most Quechua dialects (and by default in Quechua I, the branch containing Yaru/Ambo-Pasco) word stress falls on the penultimate vowel of every polysyllabic word; in Quechua I stress is word-final when the word ends in the first-person long-vowel morpheme (wasí-: 'my house'); interjections/emphatics may take final stress.
new_statements.exceptions: final stress in interjections/emphatic expressions (alaláw); Tarma and northern Junín: final stress after elision of a final syllable (aywa-mu-rá-y); Quechua I: final stress on a word-final first-person long-vowel morpheme, other final length neutralised; Pacaraos: phonemic penult/final stress; quantity-insensitive Ancash (Huaraz) and Cajatambo: initial and weight-dependent stress (Torero 1964, Parker 1976); Ferreñafe, Amazonas and 16th-c. coastal Quechua 'deviant'.
new_statements.identity_note: Adelaar & Muysken describe Quechua family-wide and Quechua I branch-wide; Ambo-Pasco Quechua (qva) is not named and falls under Torero's quantity-insensitive subgroup 'Yaru' (Andean Pasco) / Alto Pativilca-Alto Marañón-Alto Huallaga (Huánuco) on p.185. Toliver 2005 is specific to 'quechua de Ambo-Huánuco / Pasco-Pasco' but could not be opened.
